title: Weir equation coefficients (energy per litre of O2 and of CO2)
source: Weir JB, New methods for calculating metabolic rate with special reference to protein metabolism, J Physiol 1949;109:1-9 (PMC1392602 holds only scanned page images, so the coefficients below are as two later pages state the equation). Reference data for validating the energy-from-gas code; not a fit.
rows: Energy per litre of O2 in the Weir equation (protein term left out)
Full form EE = VO2 (3.941 + 1.106 RQ) (1 + 0.082 P); EE in kcal/h when VO2 is in L/h; P = protein share of total EE
Read from the validation paper's Eq 1, which attributes it to Weir 1949; with RQ = VCO2/VO2 the equation is 3.941 VO2 + 1.106 VCO2.
Energy per litre of CO2 in the Weir equation (protein term left out)
Same equation; the CO2 coefficient is the RQ term, 1.106 x (VCO2/VO2) x VO2
The page states no separate per-litre CO2 figure; 1.106 follows by substituting RQ = VCO2/VO2.
per unit protein share of EE (1 + 0.082 P)
P is the proportion of total EE from protein metabolism
Stated in the validation paper's Eq 1.
Metabolic rate (kcal per day) = 1.440 (3.9 VO2 + 1.1 VCO2), VO2 and VCO2 in L/min
Wikipedia quoting Burns and Snow; 1.440 converts L/min to per day.
Energy per litre of O2 at RQ 0.7 (low) and RQ 1.0 (high)
A cross-check of the equation: 3.941 + 1.106 x 0.7 = 4.72 and 3.941 + 1.106 = 5.05.
